evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13148.txt (sha256 b8332195..., matches; 65 FR 24595, 'Executive Order 13148 of April 21, 2000', Greening the Government Through Leadership in Environmental Management; read in full)
jobs/status-history/output/observations (Federal Register API disposition notes for the order)
FR disposition note for EO 13148: 'Revokes: EO 12088 (in part); EO 12843; EO 12856; EO 12969; Memorandum of April 26, 1994 ... Revoked by: EO 13423, January 24, 2007'
held EO 13327 and EO 13693 texts (citations of EO 13148)
reasons: All 191 quoted spans re-hashed and match the held bytes (EO_13148.txt b8332195..., EO_13423.txt 40db3c7e...). Identity agrees with the text and the Federal Register catalog record (13148, 2000-04-21, 65 FR 24595). The 94-scope inventory covers the order from the issuing paragraph to sec. 1009; the only uncovered text is page furniture. The legal theory is sound: EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(iv) revokes EO 13148 by number with no savings or effective-date wording, the FR disposition note lists EO 13423 as the only ending event, the by-number search of held order texts finds no earlier amendment or end (EO 13327 cites it; EO 13423 sec. 11(c) and EO 13693 sec. 16(d) amend EO 13327, not this order), and sec. 901 was performed on signing. The claim nonetheless gives wrong dates: the whole-order end and 93 clause ends are dated 2004-01-24, although EO 13423 was signed 2007-01-24, and sec. 901 is dated 1997-04-21, before EO 13148 was signed on 2000-04-21. The claim's own reasons give the correct dates, so it is also internally inconsistent. A claim with wrong end dates cannot be upheld even though the outcome (NO, revoked by EO 13423) is right. Minor note for correction: the earlier-end check mentions only EO 13693 sec. 16(d) as amending EO 13327's citation of this order; EO 13423 sec. 11(c) made the same amendment first.

FR disposition note for EO 13101: 'Revokes: EO 12873, October 20, 1993 / Revoked by: EO 13423, January 24, 2007 / See: EO 12843 ... Proc. 7250'
held EO 13134, EO 13148, EO 13149 texts (every citation of EO 13101 read)
packet dossier current-law leads: 48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55; 42 U.S.C. 6961 note (EO 12873 revoked by EO 13101 sec. 901)
reasons: All 173 quoted spans re-hashed and match the held bytes (EO_13101.txt 03bd381f..., EO_13423.txt 40db3c7e...). Identity agrees with the held FR text and the FR catalog record (13101, 1998-09-14, 63 FR 49643, title). The text is labelled as a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, as the transcription ruling requires. Inventory: the 85 scopes cover the order from the issuing paragraph to sec. 903 without overlap; the only uncovered text is page headers. Every operative command, including secs. 505(c), 703, 705(a)(2), 706, 801-803 and 903, is a clause. Ending: no sunset, expiry or termination-on-performance wording; the dated items (secs. 301(d), 302(a)(1), 402(d), 403(a), 503(a), 504(a), 506, 601, 702, 801(a), 903) are action deadlines, and most carry continuing duties (revise, update every 2 years, implement). EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(i) revokes EO 13101 by number. EO 13423 has no effective-date or savings wording (secs. 10 and 11 read in full), so the end is the signing date, 2007-01-24, with actor EO 13423 and mechanism express revocation, as claimed. Sec. 901 (revoking EO 12873) was performed on signing, 1998-09-14; whole_order_end equals the latest clause end. Earlier-end test: the by-number search (36 files) finds EO 13101 in order texts only in EOs 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423, and none of them amends or ends it. The FR note lists EO 13423 as the only 'Revoked by' event; its 'See' entries are orders that EO 13101 cites, plus Proc. 7250, and none ends it. Savings: EO 12873 stays revoked (consistent with the 42 U.S.C. 6961 note); EO 13693 sec. 16(a) revokes EO 13423 without revival; the CFR provisions that cite the order are agency rules and do not continue its commands; the FAR's 2007 statement that E.O. 13101 was revoked confirms the revocation. Searches are adequate and honestly described. Residual observation, not a defect: a few one-time tasks (secs. 403(a), 506, 801(a), 903) could have been exhausted by performance before 2007. No held source I read establishes their performance; EO 13148's reference to guidance issued under sec. 503 concerns a clause with a continuing duty to update. Under the evidence-decides ruling, the revocation date therefore stands as the supported first end. AI review; not certification.
